newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu ends flat, market digests reform news.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu ends flat, market digests reform news.

text.p: Romania's leu ended flat at 4,950/5,050 to the dollar on Thursday after a morning slide of about three percent, with traders still digesting news that the interbank market could be liberalised in two months.
Central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu announced plans to remove certain curbs, renewing dealer licences for several banks within the next two months.
The market now operates with only only four market-making dealer banks, all others having to observe the dealers' rates.
The restrictions, imposed by the former ruling leftists last March, were among reasons which prompted the International Monetary Fund suspend loan tranches for Romania last year.

"If this (deregulation) happens it's good news but we are waiting for words to turn into action," said one trader with a bank restricted to broker status. "Over the past year we almost forgot how a real market works," he addeed.
The former government, ousted by centrists at the polls last November, used forex curbs to prop up the local leu ahead of the elections.
During the past month the market became more flexible with the leu edging down to what many operators say is a "more realistic value".

"We are taking steps for (the creation of) a functional forex market, but we cannot say where the market will stabilise," Isarescu said. "We knew the leu was over-valued, so we have seen a rapid depreciation of the currency."
The leu has dropped some 20 percent against the dollar on the interbank market since Janury 1, with traders expecting it to suffer further loses towards 5,200/300 by the week's end.
But leu-dollar interbank rates remained still higher than retail prices which hover around 5,700/800.

"I hope more players will make the market more functional. Then we won't have to use the backdoor offered by cross trading to satisfy our clients," said a trader with one of the four selected dealer banks, three of which are state-run.
Trading in other currencies offer better prices, with quotes for the mark, French franc or others delivering at cross rates leu-dollar prices of around 5,800.
The money market ended stuck with traders awaiting the results of the refinancing auction after the BNR pushed on with tighter moves, lifting its one-week rate to 65 from 57 percent.
Keen to soak leu liquidity the BNR also slashed its offer to 1.1 trillion from a previous 2.15 trillion.
"The money market still has liquidity in excess but tighter monetary policies should soon bear fruit," said one trader.
